diagram:
flowchart TD
  SCHED["⏰ pg_cron Fridays\nUS 21:00 UTC · India 20:30 UTC"] --> MARKET["🌏 One market per run\nUS and India cohorts never mix"]
  MARKET --> CLOSED["📋 Close ORPHANED trades >14d\nno live position behind them"]
  CLOSED --> STATS["📊 Stats + champion health\ndrawdown>15% · calibration gap>0.25 · availability<60%"]
  STATS --> TOOLS["🤖 Tool loop · model from Settings\nprod: deepseek-reasoner"]
  TOOLS --> RAG["🔎 semantic_search_decisions\nJina jina-embeddings-v3 (1024-dim)"]
  TOOLS --> HYP["💡 Write hypotheses"]
  HYP --> GATE{"Ledger-only evidence · n≥10\n+ server-recomputed effect size"}
  GATE -->|"No / Phase 0 — LIVE STATE"| LOG["📝 Log only (read-only)"]
  GATE -->|"Yes"| CHALLENGER["⚖️ Create CHALLENGER\nstrategy_versions · market-scoped · ±0.05 clamp"]
  CHALLENGER --> VALID["🧪 Automated validation\nmust PASS before promotion is possible"]
  VALID --> PROMOTE["👤 Human promotes via\nStrategy Registry → champion"]

SCHED.label: Fridays · pg_cron
SCHED.description: Supabase pg_cron, NOT Windows Task Scheduler: 'kairos-learner' 0 21 * * 5 (5 PM ET) plus a separate 'kairos-learner-india' 30 20 * * 5. The route additionally gates on getDay()===5, and skips if a run already exists today for this market unless forced. Weekly avoids overfitting to noise.
SCHED.addReason: Weekly is the right learning cadence. Daily = overfit to noise.
SCHED.changeReason: Friday 5 PM verified accurate; the mechanism is pg_cron, not Windows Task Scheduler, and a second India job exists. Idempotency guard was undrawn.

MARKET.label: One market per run
MARKET.description: Each run analyzes ONE market's cohort and proposes weights ONLY for that market's champion, so a bad India run can never shift US scoring. Prod has two champions: v1.0.0 (us) and v1.0.0-india. Also loads that market's immutable trading mandate, which bounds the hold horizon it may reason about.
MARKET.addReason: The diagram had no market concept at all, which hid the blast-radius guarantee that is the whole point of the per-market split.

CLOSED.label: Close orphaned trades
CLOSED.description: Closes ORPHANED paper_trades older than 14 days — rows with no live position behind them — writing exit price, realized P&L, and outcome. It explicitly does NOT force-sell live positions on a timer: exits are fully owned by the PositionMonitor's daily deterministic checks. This is bookkeeping, not an exit policy.
CLOSED.addReason: Learning requires ground truth — actual trade outcomes.
CLOSED.changeReason: 'Closes paper_trades open >7 days' was wrong on the cutoff (14) and, more importantly, on the scope: it closes orphans only and never touches live positions.

STATS.label: Stats + champion health
STATS.description: Win rate, avg return, per-dimension correlation with P&L, plus a CHAMPION-HEALTH auto-guard — not a raw win-rate streak. It trips on drawdown >15%, calibration max-gap >0.25, or data availability <0.60.
STATS.addReason: Summary statistics needed before any weight proposal.
STATS.changeReason: The '3 runs <35% win → pause mutations' auto-guard was replaced by champion health and no longer exists in code.

TOOLS.label: Tool loop
TOOLS.description: A true tool-use agent. The model is per-flow from Settings via agent_config (prod row: deepseek-reasoner) — note the CODE fallback is still claude-opus-4-8, so only the DB row keeps Opus out of this loop. Real tools: query_signals_with_outcomes (NOT query_signals), query_score_correlation, query_macro_context, query_trade_decisions, read_priors, query_learner_config, read_past_learnings, write_hypothesis, update_signal_weight, semantic_search_decisions, and propose_feature (Phase 3 feature_registry).
TOOLS.addReason: An agent that reasons over tools evolves the strategy, vs a fixed script.
TOOLS.changeReason: Named a tool that does not exist, omitted six that do, and stated the model as fixed when it is Settings-driven with an Opus code fallback.

RAG.label: semantic_search_decisions
RAG.description: Jina jina-embeddings-v3 (1024-dim) — NOT Voyage — via the semantic_search_trade_decisions RPC over enriched trade-decision embeddings. Finds semantically similar past trades regardless of ticker to surface shared failure modes.
RAG.addReason: Keyword/filter queries miss semantically-similar situations across different symbols/regimes.
RAG.changeReason: Embedding provider was wrong: Jina, not Voyage. Retrieval goes through an RPC rather than a direct table read.

HYP.label: Write hypotheses
HYP.description: Saves grounded findings (claim + evidence + confidence + category) to learning_log for future runs.
HYP.addReason: Hypotheses accumulate into the evidence base that eventually justifies weight changes.

GATE.label: Evidence gate
GATE.description: Five gates, not two. (1) 10+ closed trades for that market — Phase 1 unlock. (2) Evidence must come from the observation_ledger; any other source is rejected outright. (3) n≥10 within the evidence itself. (4) Effect size is RE-COMPUTED server-side from the correlation — the LLM's stated confidence is not trusted. (5) Direction sanity: a weight cannot be raised when the correlation is not positive. Accepted proposals are then clamped to ±0.05 and renormalized to 1.0.
GATE.addReason: 10 trades is the minimum for statistical meaning; below that is noise.
GATE.changeReason: The 10-trade + min_confidence description understated the gate: four harder checks ship, including server-recomputed effect size that ignores the LLM's own confidence.

LOG.label: Log only
LOG.description: Phase 0: writes analysis to learning_log, no weight changes. THIS IS THE LIVE STATE — prod has 1 closed US trade and 7 closed India trades against a 10-trade gate, and zero challengers have ever been created. Every path to the right of the gate is plumbing that has never executed.
LOG.addReason: Logging builds the evidence needed to eventually tune weights.
LOG.changeReason: Verified accurate and confirmed against prod as the only path this agent has ever taken. Amended to say so, so the diagram cannot imply the challenger machinery is running.

CHALLENGER.label: Create CHALLENGER
CHALLENGER.description: Does NOT mutate live weights. Inserts an immutable strategy_versions row (state='challenger') with a weights_snapshot of only the 5 weight columns, market-scoped to the run's market, version carrying a date+HHMMSS suffix, insert errors checked. Never yet executed in prod.
CHALLENGER.addReason: Governance gate: probabilistic learning must not silently overwrite the champion strategy.
CHALLENGER.changeReason: Verified accurate; amended only to record the market scoping and that this path has never run.

VALID.label: Automated validation
VALID.description: A new challenger immediately triggers an automated validation run. It cannot be promoted until that produces a PASSED validation_experiments row — a fail-closed gate enforced in the strategy-versions route. Human promotion is necessary but NOT sufficient.
VALID.addReason: The diagram showed challenger → human → champion, implying the user's click is the only precondition. A machine gate stands in front of it.

PROMOTE.label: Human promotes
PROMOTE.description: A challenger only takes effect when the user promotes it to champion via the Strategy Registry (/dashboard/strategies), and only after validation has PASSED. Human-in-the-loop before any live strategy change — this is the one and only path by which learning reaches live scoring.
PROMOTE.addReason: Human review before learning changes live behavior.
PROMOTE.changeReason: Verified accurate and unchanged in substance; amended to record the validation precondition in front of it.

history.label: Tool loop
history.reason: Model → deepseek-reasoner (Opus had no API key)

history.label: The learner does not read [RESCORE] flags — it never did
history.reason: Added 2026-07-04 and false on the day it shipped. The learner route contains ZERO references to RESCORE. The only consumer of [RESCORE] learning_log notes is MentorCoach. The claim is doubly corroborated inside the codebase — rescore-check's own comment says 'the learner reads this' — so a reader checking the diagram against the job that writes the flags would have found the lie confirmed. Removed rather than rewired: the scoring-calibration loop this node depicted does not close through this agent, and drawing an edge for an intention is exactly the defect this audit exists to delete. The rescore→mentor path is real but belongs on MentorCoach's diagram, not here.

history.label: 14 days, ORPHANS ONLY — the learner no longer force-closes live positions
history.reason: 'Closes paper_trades open >7 days' was wrong on the number (14) and dangerously wrong on the scope. The route now skips any trade with a live position behind it and closes only ORPHANED rows — bookkeeping for trades whose position is already gone. The code states the intent directly: the LearnerAgent no longer force-sells live positions on a timer; exits are fully owned by the PositionMonitor's daily deterministic checks. The old node described a weekly LLM-adjacent job that could close your open positions on age alone, which would be a second, competing exit authority racing the monitor. It has none. This pairs with the llm_exit removal recorded on position-monitor.json the same day: both diagrams described a learner-drives-exits architecture that has been fully dismantled.

history.label: Auto-guard is champion health, not a 3-run <35% win-rate streak
history.reason: 'auto-guard check (3 runs <35% win → pause mutations)' no longer exists; the code says so in its own comment. The guard is now CHAMPION HEALTH and trips on any of: drawdown >15%, calibration max-gap >0.25, or data availability <0.60. Not a wording change — the old rule keyed on a small-sample win-rate streak, which on a book with 1 closed US trade is pure noise, while the new rule keys on the champion's realized drawdown, its probability calibration, and whether the evidence feeding it is even present. Availability <0.60 is the notable addition: the guard now trips on STARVED EVIDENCE, meaning the learner refuses to learn from a cohort scored on absent data rather than confidently learning the wrong thing from it.

history.label: Embeddings are Jina jina-embeddings-v3, not Voyage voyage-finance-2
history.reason: The provider was wrong. Retrieval runs on Jina (jina-embeddings-v3, 1024-dim, JINA_API_KEY) via the semantic_search_trade_decisions RPC — not Voyage, and not a direct table read. Worth recording that the diagram was not the only liar here: the learner's OWN tool description in code still advertises 'using Voyage AI embeddings' to the model at runtime, so the stale claim is also being fed to the LLM. That is a code defect, reported and NOT fixed (documentation-only task). The dimension (1024) and the purpose — find semantically similar past trades regardless of ticker to surface shared failure modes — are verified accurate and unchanged.

history.label: query_signals does not exist; six tools were undrawn; model is Settings-driven with an Opus code fallback
history.reason: Three corrections. (1) query_signals is not a tool — it is query_signals_with_outcomes; anyone tracing the loop by tool name would find nothing. (2) Six tools were missing: query_learner_config, read_past_learnings, write_hypothesis, update_signal_weight, semantic_search_decisions, and propose_feature — the last being a Phase 3 feature_registry capability, i.e. the learner can propose new FEATURES, not just weights, and the diagram gave no hint such a surface exists. (3) The 2026-07-04 note 'deepseek-reasoner (NOT Opus — the app has no ANTHROPIC_API_KEY)' is true in PROD but false as an architectural claim: the model is per-flow from agent_config, and the code's fallback is STILL claude-opus-4-8. Only the DB row keeps Opus out of this loop — delete that row and the stated impossibility becomes the default. Verified against the prod agent_config row rather than assumed.

history.label: Five gates, not two — and the LLM's own confidence is not trusted
history.reason: '10+ closed trades, per-dimension min_confidence, no auto-guard trip' understated the gate in the direction that matters. The real stack: (1) 10+ closed trades for that market; (2) evidence must originate from the observation_ledger — any other source is rejected outright; (3) n≥10 within the evidence itself; (4) effect size is RE-COMPUTED server-side from the correlation rather than taken from the model — the LLM's stated confidence is explicitly not trusted, which is the opposite of what 'min_confidence' implies; (5) direction sanity — a weight cannot be raised when the correlation is not positive. Survivors are then clamped to ±0.05 and renormalized to 1.0, so no single run can lurch the strategy. This is the most under-sold part of the whole diagram: the governance is materially stronger than advertised, and describing it as a confidence threshold made a probabilistic-trust story out of a deterministic one.

history.label: Per-market cohorts + champions — the diagram had no market concept
history.reason: Shipped and undrawn. Each run analyzes ONE market's cohort and proposes weights ONLY for that market's champion; every query is market-scoped. The code names the guarantee: a bad India run can never shift US scoring. Prod confirms two live champions (v1.0.0 us, v1.0.0-india), both still seeded Phase-0 baselines with identical weights. Given its own node because a single-cohort mental model would suggest 8 closed trades across both markets nearly clears the 10-trade gate, when in reality the gate sees 1 (US) and 7 (India) separately — neither close. Also recorded the per-market trading mandate load and the same-day idempotency guard on SCHED, both undrawn.

history.label: Automated validation must PASS before a challenger can be promoted
history.reason: The diagram drew challenger → human promotes → champion, implying the user's click is the only thing standing between a proposed weight change and live scoring. It is not: a new challenger immediately triggers an automated validation run, and the strategy-versions route FAILS CLOSED unless a PASSED validation_experiments row exists. Human approval is necessary but not sufficient. Drawn because this diagram feeds the one path by which learning reaches live money (the research WEIGHTS node), and understating the gate in front of it is the same class of error as paper-trader's fictional approval gate — just in the safer direction. PROMOTE and CHALLENGER were otherwise verified ACCURATE and kept: immutable row, state='challenger', 5-column weights_snapshot, date+HHMMSS version suffix, errors checked, no live mutation.

history.label: Verified accurate — and confirmed against prod as the ONLY path ever taken
history.reason: 'Phase 0: writes analysis to learning_log, no weight changes' is TRUE and unchanged. Verified against prod rather than assumed: paper_trades shows 1 closed US trade and 7 closed India trades against a per-market 10-trade gate, and strategy_versions holds exactly 2 rows — both seeded champions, is_champion=true, ZERO challengers ever created. So every node to the right of the gate is plumbing that has never executed, and the entire live behaviour of this agent is: read, analyze, log. Amended the description to state this explicitly, because a diagram that draws the challenger→validation→promotion chain in the same visual weight as the log-only path implies a learning loop that is running. It is not — it is waiting for trades. SCHED's Friday 5 PM claim also verified accurate (pg_cron 0 21 * * 5); only its Windows Task Scheduler mechanism was wrong, plus the undrawn India job at 20:30 UTC.
